survey:
Image 4 is a sci-fi control console standing on a riveted metal floor. It is a light-grey box seen from slightly above and to the right. The front face is wide and holds an inset drawer with a centred dark handle. A narrow shaded right side face recedes up and to the right. The top is a sloped dark-grey panel that tilts up toward the camera, with a raised grey rail across its back edge. On the panel are two round gauges (a large white one and a smaller green one), eight round buttons in two staggered rows of four, and a vertical lever with a red ball knob. The lever rises from a rectangular slotted base on the right of the panel.

The front face's top and bottom edges, the drawer edges, the panel's lower edge and the back rail all slope gently down to the right. They converge toward the left, which fits a right end nearer the viewer. The side face's bottom edge climbs steeply toward a second vanishing point on the right, so the box reads as consistent two-point perspective. Verticals stay vertical.

The gauge and button rims are ellipses squashed by about the same amount, which suits the panel's tilt. The button rows run parallel to the panel's edges. The lever stands upright, and its slot base is seen from the same raised view as the panel. The box's bottom edge sits flush on the floor and runs parallel to the nearest floor seam. The floor seams and rivets lie in the same plane as the box base.

All parts agree on one camera. The only slight looseness is that the buttons on the nearer right are barely larger than those on the left. That is within mild stylized perspective and not worth reporting.
